skill.name: wezterm
skill.description: Control WezTerm terminal panes, tabs, workspaces, and windows through documented CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Use WezTerm CLI commands to inspect and manage terminal panes, tabs, workspaces, and windows.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks and fenced WezTerm CLI examples rather than executable Ruby code. The skill still documents terminal-control workflows, including sending newline-terminated text into panes, so the main residual risk is accidental command execution in local or SSH sessions.

remediation.issue: Send-text workflows can execute commands in existing terminal sessions.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation of target pane, domain, command text, and newline behavior before any send-text use.

remediation.issue: CLI examples are presented without explicit safety boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to list panes first, avoid destructive commands, and separate local sessions from SSH sessions.

remediation.issue: The configuration file path is shown without access guidance.
remediation.suggestion: State that the WezTerm configuration file should be read or edited only after a direct user request.

static_findings.snippet: Use the `wezterm` CLI to control and interact with WezTerm terminal instances.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Terminal Input Capability
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs assistants to send text containing a newline into current or selected WezTerm panes. This can execute commands in active local or SSH terminal sessions if used without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The send-text examples explicitly include newline-terminated shell input, and the file also documents SSH domain spawning. This is a legitimate feature, but it creates clear command-execution risk in existing terminal sessions.

content.value_statement: Managing terminal panes and workspaces manually slows AI-assisted development. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured WezTerm CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: List WezTerm panes, clients, domains, and workspaces.
Create, split, focus, zoom, and activate panes.
Create and navigate tabs by index or relative position.
Send text to current or selected WezTerm panes.
Start WezTerm windows with commands or working directories.
Reference the standard WezTerm configuration file location.
limitations: Requires the WezTerm CLI to be installed and accessible.
Does not validate pane IDs, tab indexes, or command safety.
Does not include scripts, wrappers, or automatic error handling.
Commands can affect active local or remote terminal sessions.

use_cases.title: Organize Development Sessions
use_cases.description: Create panes and tabs for editors, logs, shells, and monitoring views inside one WezTerm workspace.

use_cases.title: Inspect Terminal Layouts
use_cases.description: List panes, clients, workspaces, and domains before choosing where an assistant should act.

use_cases.title: Manage Remote Workflows
use_cases.description: Connect WezTerm sessions to configured SSH domains and keep local and remote terminal contexts visible.

prompt_templates.title: List My Panes
prompt_templates.prompt: List my current WezTerm panes and summarize the workspace, domain, and active pane context.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Focused Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a WezTerm layout with one editor pane and one terminal pane, then tell me which pane is active.

prompt_templates.title: Navigate Existing Tabs
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my WezTerm tabs, switch to the next useful tab, and report the selected tab and pane.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Local And Remote Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my WezTerm domains, identify local and SSH sessions, and prepare a safe plan before sending any terminal input.

output_examples.input: Find my open WezTerm panes and describe the current workspace.
output_examples.output: A concise pane inventory with workspace names, pane identifiers, domains, and the active window context.

output_examples.input: Split my terminal and start a monitoring view in the new pane.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates a new pane, starts the requested monitoring view, and reports the new pane identifier.

output_examples.input: Prepare to send text to a remote pane.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the target pane, domain, and command text before any input is sent.

best_practices: Confirm the target pane or tab before sending text with a newline.
Use read-only listing commands before changing terminal layouts.
Keep remote SSH domains separate from local workflow automation.
anti_patterns: Sending destructive commands to a pane without explicit user approval.
Assuming the current pane is safe for automated input.
Using placeholder pane IDs or paths without checking current state.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It documents WezTerm CLI workflows for panes, tabs, workspaces, domains, windows, and basic configuration discovery.

faq.question: Does it install WezTerm?
faq.answer: No. WezTerm must already be installed, and its CLI must be available to the assistant environment.

faq.question: Can it send commands into a terminal?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes send-text workflows, so users should confirm the pane and command before execution.

faq.question: Can it manage SSH sessions?
faq.answer: It can reference configured WezTerm SSH domains, but it does not create credentials or configure remote access.

faq.question: Does it parse command output automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides CLI examples, but parsing and error handling must be handled by the assistant or user.

faq.question: Is it safe for unattended automation?
faq.answer: No. Terminal control should stay supervised because commands can affect active shells and remote sessions.
